title: Identifying Risk Variables From Raw ESG Data Using Its Hierarchical Structure

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a Hierarchical Variable Selection (HVS) framework to identify raw Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) variables relevant to financial risk, measured by the logarithmic volatility of returns. The methodology involves a multi-stage feature selection process: first performing stepwise regressions within each ESG category of the LSEG hierarchical structure, then running a consolidated stepwise regression across all significant variables, and finally applying Ridge regression with 5-fold cross-validation to enhance out-of-sample robustness and assess relative variable importance.
extraction.universe: Company data from various sectors of the US economy, including S&P 500 and Russell 2000 constituents
key_findings: Using raw ESG variables directly in feature selection provides significantly stronger explanatory power for financial risk than relying on aggregated ESG scores.
Logarithmic transformation of return volatility effectively addresses heteroskedasticity and right-skewness in residuals.
HVS-selected ESG variables provide incremental explanatory power even in the presence of traditional financial risk factors.

Relevant ESG risk variables differ substantially between large-cap and small-cap companies within the same sector (e.g., environmental factors dominate large energy firms, while social and governance factors dominate small ones).
limitations: ESG datasets frequently contain missing values and high sparsity, necessitating careful data processing and imputation assumptions.
Feature selection models applied to high-dimensional datasets are prone to overfitting without regularization steps like Ridge regression.
